title: Who we spend our day with, and how it changes as we age

detailIdle.title: Hover over a dot or group
detailIdle.body: Hover over a dot to see how one person spent all 24 hours, or over a group on the left to see who it includes.

detailHint: Each dot is a survey respondent, resampled by survey weight.

endCard.title: Your turn
endCard.text: Play any hour of the day yourself, or switch to the hours-by-age chart, in Explore.

notes: Each dot is a survey respondent resampled in proportion to their survey weight; dots are not tracked individuals.
ATUS does not ask who was present during sleep, grooming, work, or class.
When several people were present, the dot joins one group in this order: children, partner, other family, friends, others.
2020–2021 are excluded because the pandemic disrupted normal social time.

Time alone is not the same as loneliness: the survey records who was present, not how people felt. The comparison of loneliness to smoking comes from the U.S. Surgeon General's 2023 advisory, Our Epidemic of Loneliness and Isolation.

sources.label: American Time Use Survey, 2003–2025 multi-year microdata, U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics

groupInfo.partner: With a spouse or unmarried partner. If their children were there too, the dot goes to Your children.
groupInfo.children: With their own children: kids living at home (of any age), foster children, or their own children under 18 living elsewhere.
groupInfo.family: With other relatives: parents, brothers and sisters, grandchildren, in-laws and other family.
groupInfo.others: With anyone else: coworkers outside of working time, neighbors, housemates, customers and other people.
groupInfo.work: Working or in class. The survey doesn't ask who people are with during these, so the dots are gray.
groupInfo.sleep: Sleeping, grooming and other personal care. The survey doesn't ask who people are with during these, so the dots are gray.
